prompt: What is a DNS zone?
options: An administratively managed portion of the DNS namespace
A network adapter with a static IP
A list of all devices on a switch
A password database for domain users
en: A zone groups DNS data under an administrative boundary; a server can host multiple zones.
ru: Zone DNS namespace ka managed hissa hai; aik server multiple zones host kar sakta hai.

prompt: In a standard file-backed primary/secondary design, where are zone records directly maintained?
options: On the writable primary zone
On any secondary copy
Only inside the client resolver cache
On a stub instead of the primary
en: The standard primary is the writable source. Secondary copies receive changes through transfer.
ru: Standard primary writable source hai; secondary changes transfer se leta hai.

prompt: What does a secondary zone contain?
options: A complete read-only copy of the zone
Only the IP addresses of forwarders
Only the most recently queried record
Only authority metadata without host records
en: A secondary holds the full zone data as a read-only authoritative copy.
ru: Secondary ke paas full read-only authoritative zone copy hoti hai.

prompt: What is the main purpose of a stub zone?
options: Help a resolver locate the zone’s authoritative servers
Provide an independent full copy of every host record
Apply Group Policy to domain computers
Allocate IP addresses to new clients
en: A stub maintains limited authority information rather than the complete ordinary record set.
ru: Stub limited authority information rakhta hai, tamam host records nahin.

prompt: Which collection best describes stub-zone contents?
options: SOA, NS and necessary address/glue records
Every A, CNAME and PTR record in the full zone
Only MX records and mail-server passwords
Client routing tables and default gateways
en: The stub identifies authorities. Multiple entries may exist; it is not exactly three individual records.
ru: Stub authorities identify karta hai; multiple entries ho sakti hain, sirf teen records lazmi nahin.

prompt: What is a zone transfer used for?
options: Replicating zone data between DNS servers
Joining a workstation to Active Directory
Changing a VM’s port group
Encrypting a DNS client’s password
en: Zone transfer supplies replicated DNS data; it is separate from domain membership and networking changes.
ru: Zone transfer DNS data copy karta hai; domain join aur network changes alag hain.

prompt: Which statement about server and zone roles is accurate?
options: One server can be primary for one zone and secondary for another
A machine labelled primary must be primary for every zone
A secondary cannot host any other zone
A stub role is permanently fixed to the hardware
en: The role is specific to a hosted zone, not a permanent identity of the whole machine.
ru: Role hosted zone ka hai, poori machine ki permanent pehchan nahin.

prompt: What does a forward lookup normally seek?
options: An address associated with a DNS name
The physical switch port for a MAC address
The name associated with an IP via PTR
The current password of the named server
en: Forward lookup resolves names to addresses; reverse PTR lookup answers the opposite naming question.
ru: Forward naam se address, reverse PTR IP se naam poochta hai.

prompt: Which record is used for an address-to-name reverse lookup?
options: PTR
CNAME
MX
TXT
en: PTR records belong to the reverse namespace and associate an address with a name.
ru: PTR reverse namespace mein address ko naam se associate karta hai.

prompt: How do suitable writable replicas of an AD-integrated zone replicate zone data?
options: Through Active Directory replication
Only through standard primary-to-secondary transfers
By requiring every client to copy the zone
By converting all replicas into read-only stubs
en: AD-integrated storage uses AD replication; it is different from the standard file-backed model.
ru: AD-integrated storage AD replication use karti hai; standard file-backed model se alag hai.

prompt: DNS01 (.121) is primary. DNS02 (.122) is secondary. A user queries DNS02 for an existing record. How can DNS02 answer?
options: From its own valid full zone copy
It must ask DNS01 on every query
It must first become a domain controller
It must copy the entire zone for every request
en: A secondary can answer locally from its existing valid copy.
ru: Secondary apni existing valid copy se locally jawab de sakta hai.

prompt: DNS01 is temporarily offline. DNS02 is reachable and its secondary copy is still valid. What is expected for existing records?
options: DNS02 can answer without promotion
DNS02 must be promoted before any answer
DNS02 must remove its zone immediately
DNS02 must turn its full copy into a stub
en: Availability of existing records does not require converting the secondary into a writable primary.
ru: Existing records serve karne ke liye secondary ko writable primary banana zaroori nahin.

prompt: You add an A record for DNS02 on DNS01. What has this action accomplished by itself?
options: Created a name-to-address mapping in that zone
Installed the DNS role on DNS02
Created a secondary zone on DNS02
Enabled automatic failover between both servers
en: A host record is data. It does not configure the service or zone role on the named machine.
ru: Host record data hai; named machine par DNS service ya zone role configure nahin karta.

prompt: DNS03 has a stub for VCPLAB.Com. Its required authorities are unreachable and it has no usable cached answer for a requested host. What follows?
options: It cannot resolve that missing host from the stub alone
It reads the host from its full secondary copy
It automatically creates an authoritative A record
It returns the primary server’s IP for every host
en: Authority metadata is not the complete host list. A missing answer still needs a reachable source.
ru: Authority metadata full host list nahin; missing answer ke liye reachable source chahiye.

prompt: All three lab servers return .122 for dns02.vcplab.com. What can you conclude?
options: The name resolved through each tested server at that time
All three store identical full zone copies
All three have writable primary zones
Automatic failover has been fully verified
en: The same client-visible answer can come from different storage and resolver roles.
ru: Same answer mukhtalif storage aur resolver roles se aa sakta hai.

prompt: Two DNS VMs run on the same ESXi host. What shared risk remains?
options: A host failure can stop both DNS VMs
A primary zone cannot run in a VM
A secondary must always run on physical hardware
Each DNS VM automatically moves to a different site
en: Separate VMs still share the hypervisor host as a failure dependency.
ru: Alag VMs phir bhi aik hypervisor host ki failure par depend karti hain.

prompt: You create a forward zone on DNS01. What is true about reverse DNS?
options: Its reverse zone and PTR records require separate configuration
All reverse records now exist automatically
The forward zone becomes read-only
Reverse queries no longer use DNS
en: Forward and reverse namespaces are separate. Creation of a forward zone alone does not complete reverse setup.
ru: Forward aur reverse namespaces alag hain; forward zone akeli reverse setup complete nahin karti.

prompt: A client lists DNS02 as its preferred DNS server. Does this setting define the hosted zone’s role?
options: No; it selects a resolver, independently of the zone role
Yes; preferred always means writable primary
Yes; preferred always means secondary
Yes; preferred converts all zones into stubs
en: Client resolver selection and a server’s hosted zone roles are different settings.
ru: Client resolver selection aur hosted zone roles alag settings hain.

prompt: A standard secondary zone must become writable after permanent loss of its primary. What is the appropriate interpretation?
options: An administrator can plan a conversion and handle the old primary’s return
It automatically becomes writable as soon as one query fails
Its clients can edit the secondary directly without any change
A stub must be created before existing records can be read
en: Promotion/conversion is an administrative recovery action and needs consistency planning.
ru: Conversion administrative recovery action hai; consistency planning chahiye.

prompt: A poster shows www, mail and db records, but no lab evidence establishes those entries. How should they be treated?
options: Illustrative examples, not confirmed lab configuration
Proof those records exist on DNS01
Proof DNS02 transferred those specific records
Evidence that the printer and mail services are reachable
en: Educational illustrations are not captured configuration evidence.
ru: Educational illustration captured configuration evidence nahin hoti.

prompt: DNS02 is missing a newly added record. What is the best focused investigation?
options: Compare zone serials and inspect master, transfer permissions and connectivity
Rename DNS02 until its hostname matches the record
Delete the reverse zone as the first action
Change every client’s default gateway immediately
en: Stale secondary data calls for transfer/update checks, not unrelated naming or routing changes.
ru: Stale secondary data mein transfer/update checks chahiye, unrelated changes nahin.

prompt: A secondary cannot refresh for longer than its zone expiry interval. What is the key concern?
options: The expired zone copy cannot be served indefinitely
Expiry converts the copy into a writable primary
Expiry is identical to every record’s cache TTL
Expiry guarantees that a stub takes over the full data
en: SOA expiry limits serving a stale secondary copy; it is distinct from record-cache TTL.
ru: SOA expiry stale secondary copy serve karne ki had hai; record-cache TTL se alag hai.

prompt: After editing DNS01, an administrator sees a Notify configuration and claims DNS02 has the update. What evidence is still needed?
options: Verify the new data or relevant version on DNS02
Only confirm that the Notify button exists
Only query an unrelated public website
Only check that DNS01 has an A record for itself
en: Notification prompts checking. It is not evidence that the transfer succeeded.
ru: Notify check ka paigham hai; successful transfer ki evidence nahin.

prompt: An internal-name query receives a valid NXDOMAIN. Which expectation is mistaken?
options: Every alternate resolver must now be queried until one returns an address
The name’s spelling and selected zone should be checked
The chosen server returned a negative DNS response
The queried namespace might differ from the intended one
en: A valid negative reply is different from no reply; normal fallback is not a search for a preferred answer.
ru: Valid negative reply aur no reply alag hain; fallback pasand ka answer dhoondna nahin.

prompt: A correct A answer is returned, but the application still cannot connect. What should be checked next?
options: Application service, port reachability and access controls
Assume successful DNS proves the application is running
Convert the forward zone into a reverse zone
Promote the secondary just to open the application port
en: Name resolution is one layer. It does not prove transport or application access.
ru: Name resolution aik layer hai; transport ya application access ka proof nahin.
